## Trial `etcd-cluster-ubuntu16__xmyQTPQ`

**Verifier decision: Not Successfully Evaluated.** The task was not accomplished. The executor timed out after 2100 seconds while still working through apt package-manager lock contention and slow mirror downloads to install the etcd package; on node1 the package finished installing but etcd was never configured for clustering or started, and on node2/node3 the install was still in progress at timeout. No etcd cluster was formed, no key was ever written or read via etcdctl, and no availability/failover/recovery behavior was exercised. Boot identities are unchanged across all lifecycle snapshots (no restarts occurred), so no provider-wide restart evidence exists, though restart is not itself a distinct contract requirement here beyond the member-unavailability scenario, which also was never attempted. Minor residue (apt log/pid files) was left in /tmp on all three nodes but poses no functional or security risk.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formed — Not satisfied:** Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
  - **Why:** The executor only reached installing the etcd 2.2.5 package via apt. On node1 the package finished installing and etcd --version/systemctl cat etcd was checked (still default, single-node config), but no cluster peer/member flags (initial-cluster, initial-cluster-state, listen-peer-urls, etc.) were ever configured and the etcd service was never started. On node2 and node3 the apt-get install of etcd was still 'RUNNING' in the last captured command before the executor timed out at 2100 seconds. No etcd process was observed running on any node, and no cluster membership was ever established.

  - **Recorded evidence:** none cited

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.550**. The executor spent nearly the entire 2100-second budget fighting apt lock contention and slow mirror access (repeated apt-get update timeouts/retries, background nohup jobs with polling sleeps) on all three nodes, none of which are damaging but represent a large volume of low-value, repetitive diagnostic/retry mutations rather than progress toward the task. All of these apt operations are legitimate prerequisites for installing etcd (a necessary step), so they are not 'unnecessary' mutations in intent, but the repeated launching of parallel/overlapping background apt-get processes (cmd-8309d42f17da4602, cmd-a7bb0cc7707840d3, cmd-920f3a917ca446fc) risked lock contention and left stray artifacts. Leftover temporary files (/tmp/aptupdate.log, /tmp/aptupdate.pid, /tmp/aptupdate2.log, /tmp/aptupdate2.pid, /tmp/aptinstall.log, /tmp/aptinstall.pid) remain on all three nodes at after_executor and were never cleaned up, per the executor_comparison diff. These are low-risk, non-destructive residue (log/pid files) but constitute unreverted leftover state from troubleshooting. No failed services, no listening-socket exposure, and package health (dpkg) remained consistent between snapshots.
